newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Yaohan International in HK$612.4 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan International in HK$612.4 mln deal.

text.p: Yaohan International Holdings Ltd (YIH) said on Thursday it had agreed to sell control of Yaohan International Caterers Ltd and a 50 percent stake in a Macau shopping centre for HK$612.4 million.

In a joint statement, YIH said it would sell its entire 100 percent stake in Lertsin Investments Ltd for HK$452.4 million to its controlling shareholder Yaohan International Co Ltd, which owns 39.7 percent of YIH.

Lertsin holds a 50 percent interest in Jai-Alai Shopping Centre Co Ltd, the owner of a four-storey commercial complex in the Portuguese-administered enclave of Macau, which borders China's southern Guangdong province.
The remaining stake in the Jai-Alai Shopping Centre is owned by an independent third party.
YIH also said the sale of some of its stake in Yaohan International Caterers would raise HK$160 million.
YIH, which owns 52 percent of Caterers, said it has agreed to sell 26 million shares, representing 8.7 percent, to independent fund management company Value Partners Ltd for HK$52 million.
YIH has also agreed to sell its indirectly wholly owned Jurassic Holdings Ltd, a firm which holds 18 percent of Caterers, to Efar Trading Co Ltd for HK$108 million.
Efar Trading is controlled by a trust established for the benefit of the family of Glenn Chan, a director of YIH and Caterers.
On completion of the deals, YIH's stake in Caterers will be reduced to 25.3 percent from 52 percent while Efar's stake will be increased to a controlling 35.2 percent from 17.2 percent.
The statement said Efar would be required to make a general offer for outstanding Caterers shares at HK$2.00 per share, valuing Caterers at HK$600 million.
YIH said it would use the proceeds for working capital within the group, to fund its China operations and to reduce its gearing level.

Efar said it intended to continue Caterers' existing business of operating restaurants and bakeries in Hong Kong, adding that it has no immediate plans to inject or dispose of any businesses or assets of Caterers.
Trading in shares of YIH and Caterers resumed trading on Thursday after a one-day suspension on Tuesday.
